name: WHO emergencies
summary: WHO's Bundibugyo Ebola emergency of international concern, declared 17 May, remains in force; no new PHEIC found
state: WHO declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May, and its IHR Emergency Committee issued updated temporary recommendations on 24 Aug (WHO). WHO's Disease Outbreak News of 6 Nov covers the continued response, and searches to 15 Nov found no new PHEIC in the past 30 days and no pandemic emergency. A PHEIC in effect keeps the level at Watch.
for_you: The emergency mainly affects people living in or travelling to DR Congo and neighbouring countries. Check FCDO travel advice and the NHS Fit for Travel pages before travel to the region.
rubric_hit: Watch: a PHEIC in effect (Ebola, declared 17 May); no new PHEIC in past 30 days
basis_detail: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)
basis_by: WHO (PHEIC and IHR Emergency Committee decisions)

why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.
